newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda denies backing raids into eastern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda denies backing raids into eastern Zaire.

text.p: Rwanda denied on Monday backing cross-border raids into eastern Zaire by Tutsi infiltrators while an influx of refugees from the troubled region reported heavy fighting.
Zaire said on Friday its troops clashed with armed groups of Banyamulenge Tutsi infiltrators and accused neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi of raising tension by backing cross-border raids.
"These statements are basically a lie," said Rwandan military spokesman Emmanuel Ndahiro on Monday. "The Zairean government is transferring its responsibility to others."

"Zaire has not been able to contain the insecurity within its own borders caused by criminals from Rwanda. Zaire should settle down and respond to its own problems and comply with agreements with our country," he added in the capital Kigali.
A spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Kigali said a total of 411 refugees had crossed into southwestern Rwanda from eastern Zaire since Sunday night.
UNHCR spokesman Khassim Diagne said the refugees crossed into Cyangugu province and all reported they were fleeing violence around Luberizi, north of the border town of Uvira.

"THese Banyamulenge claim they were rounded up in the Uvira area, jailed, robbed, attacked, manhandled and starved. They are almost all Tutsis. All report fighting in and around Rusizi plain," he said.

The Zairean government said on Friday Banyamulenge had infiltrated from Rwanda and killed dozens of Zaireans in the east since the start of the month. It confirmed reports from U.N. aid officials of clashes with troops in the Uvira region.
The Banyamulenge are mostly Tutsis originally of Rwandan origin who have lived in eastern Zaire for decades or more.

Their poor relations with local Zairean tribes and the Zairean army worsened with the arrival of more than a million Rwandan Hutus who fled Rwanda after the 1994 killing of up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus by Hutu extremists before Tutsi rebels took power.
